reviews.review:
Not a complex game, but fun and stylish. The level design and story progression are completely linear, and all visuals and dialogues are set in the cliché universe of Warhammer 40k - however, I like that dystopic sci-fi world. The game is not very hard either, as soon as you understood which weapon to use in certain tactical situations and when to pop your fury buff. A special mechanic is how to regenerate health: Not some food or med kits lying around guarantee your survival, but executing stunned monsters in close combat, which means that your regeneration is not handed out to you, you have to work for it, and I like that, too. 

The most remarkable thing about this particular W40k game, apart from the excellent sound effects and voice acting, is your character. It is not a story of "rising from nothing" and becoming a great hero - you already start as one. You are a captain of the Ultramarines, the genetically enhanced elite force of the Emperor in his war against the enemies of mankind, aliens and demons. You are a respected leader amongst your battle brothers, and as every Space Marine has a part of the Emperor himself in his genes, common humans in the Imperial army refer to you as "My Lord" and bend their knees to you. This setting makes it plausible that you are an invincible power armored fighting machine who can single-handedly defeat hordes of opponents with your arsenal of ranged and melee weapons. Plausability is good for immersion, and besides, it feels good to be revered a little!

I was a bit underwhelmed by the final boss fight. After several waves of mobs you already encountered before, you switch to a falling scenario and press buttons prompted to you on the screen. You win by - clicking your mouse as fast as you can. That feels cheap and breaks the immersion almost completely. 

With a little more variety in regard to the mobs and a more creative ending, this game could have been very good - like this, it is just "good enough": 6.5/10 from me, for the solo campaign. I have not tried multiplayer yet and cannot comment on that part of the game.
Best 40K fps/3ps ever. Runs flawlessly, huge amounts of violence, impressive backdrop. If only they could just have taken this and put it online: this is what Eternal Crusade should be like!
If any game deserves a sequel, it is this one!

DON'T expect: Innovative, mind-blowing, genre-redefining game

Do expect: a decent actiony 3rd person shooter with hack'n'slash elements where you get to feel like a demigod. I'm not that into 40k lore but from what I can gather, the developers did some good fan service with this game so there's that too

8/10 would recommend
